evaluation_dimensions.name: Architecture
evaluation_dimensions.description: Technical stack, modularity, micro‑service vs. monolith, API extensibility, and integration points with existing enterprise ecosystems. [[DOC-001]]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Enterprise Latency / Throughput
evaluation_dimensions.description: Measured end‑to‑end processing latency, concurrent request handling capacity, and scalability limits under production workloads. [[DOC-002]]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Pricing Predictability
evaluation_dimensions.description: Clarity of pricing tiers, usage‑based vs. flat‑rate models, hidden fees, and cost‑simulation tools for capacity planning. [[DOC-003]]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Advertised vs. Actual SLA
evaluation_dimensions.description: Comparison of published service‑level agreements (uptime, response time, support) against real‑world performance data and breach incidents. [[DOC-004]]

evaluation_dimensions.name: On-Prem / Hybrid Readiness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Availability of on‑premise, edge, or hybrid deployment options, data residency controls, and orchestration compatibility (Kubernetes, OpenShift). [[DOC-005]]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Customer Sentiment & Trust
evaluation_dimensions.description: Aggregate sentiment from G2 reviews, Net Promoter Scores, social listening, and qualitative feedback on trust, support quality, and roadmap confidence. [[DOC-006]]

sources.purpose: Quantitative sentiment scores, qualitative comment extraction, and trend analysis across the four vendors.
Capture advertised architecture diagrams, pricing tables, SLA clauses, and hybrid deployment statements.
Independent validation of performance benchmarks, market positioning, and implementation friction.
First‑hand accounts of deployment challenges, support experiences, and perceived value.

sources.type: Support Ticket & Incident Logs (publicly disclosed or via partner access)
sources.purpose: Measure actual SLA adherence and identify recurring operational pain points.
Detect undocumented integration issues and real‑world troubleshooting patterns.

actions: Create a rubric for sentiment polarity (positive, neutral, negative).
Map pricing elements to a cost‑model template.
Use G2 API to pull the latest 200 reviews per competitor.
Scrape vendor pricing pages with a headless browser.
Extract SLA language via PDF parsing tools.
Normalize latency figures to a common workload (e.g., 1 TB batch ingest).
Convert pricing to $/CPU‑hour and $/TB‑stored for cross‑vendor comparability.
Tag each review with sentiment tags using a pretrained NLP model.
Conduct 8–10 semi‑structured interviews with current customers of each vendor.
Cross‑check interview insights against public incident reports.
Score each dimension on a 1‑5 scale using weighted averages (e.g., 30% sentiment, 25% SLA adherence).
Generate a heat‑map matrix to visualize comparative strengths/weaknesses.
Produce a benchmark deck with executive summary, methodology appendix, and raw data repository.
Highlight implementation friction hotspots and mitigation tactics for each competitor.

competitor_profiles.name: CloudScale AI
competitor_profiles.positioning: Enterprise‑grade LLM gateway and multi‑model orchestration platform targeting mid‑to‑large engineering enterprises that need to productionize multi‑agent systems.

competitor_profiles.name: DataPulse Systems
competitor_profiles.positioning: Real‑time streaming data infrastructure and feature‑store for autonomous agents, aimed at financial institutions, fraud‑detection teams, and high‑frequency analytics workloads.

competitor_profiles.name: NexusOps Technologies
competitor_profiles.positioning: Autonomous AIOps platform that correlates telemetry and drives self‑healing incident workflows for DevOps, SRE, and platform‑engineering teams managing large‑scale Kubernetes environments.

competitor_profiles.name: Veloce Security
competitor_profiles.positioning: GenAI runtime firewall that defends against prompt injection, jailbreaks, and PII leakage, serving healthcare, legal, and other compliance‑sensitive enterprises running LLMs on private data.
